summary: The application attracted sustained opposition from October 2025, led by APRS with a local residents' campaign group (WhatsApp/Instagram based), and protests outside the City Chambers before the 4 February 2026 committee hearing. Concerns centred on climate impact and 'greenwashing' of the green data centre label, the decision not to require an EIA, diesel backup generators near planned housing and a nursery, energy/grid demand, and minimal job creation against the mixed-use vision for Edinburgh Park. Councillors from all parties echoed these concerns and refused unanimously against officer advice. At appeal, 38 representations were lodged with the DPEA, including from APRS and ERCS Legal. The appellant confirmed on 12 August 2026 that it would submit an EIA Report, and Scottish Ministers recalled the appeal on 17 August for their own consideration.

principal_concerns.concern: Climate impact and lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions of a c. 210-213 MW facility; Cockburn Association-reported analysis put projected annual emissions at roughly 200,000 tonnes CO2, compared to about 10% of Edinburgh's total
principal_concerns.raised_by: APRS, councillors (refusal grounds cite NPF4 Policies 1 and 2), Cockburn Association

principal_concerns.concern: 'Greenwashing': no statutory definition of a 'green data centre'; renewable power supply asserted but no figures provided; limited reassurance on cooling efficiency; no pre-engagement with Scottish Water on water use; doubts over deliverability of waste heat re-use
principal_concerns.raised_by: Cllr Alys Mumford and other committee members; APRS ('Olympic-level greenwashing')
principal_concerns.developer_response: Shelborn argued the scheme met NPF4 green data centre criteria and that waste heat could supply future Edinburgh Park homes and offices

principal_concerns.concern: Decision not to require an Environmental Impact Assessment despite the scale of energy use, described by APRS as 'gobsmacking'
principal_concerns.raised_by: APRS; also pursued at appeal (Finch UKSC ruling cited)
principal_concerns.developer_response: The appellant confirmed to DPEA on 12 August 2026 that it will submit an EIA Report; Scottish Ministers recalled the appeal five days later.

principal_concerns.concern: Diesel standby generators: emissions ('100,000 idling cars-worth of diesel' if run at scale), testing, noise and flue stacks, on a site 220 m from a nursery, upwind of the city centre and c. 50 m from a consented housing development

Conflict with City Plan 2030 Place 19 mixed-use vision for Edinburgh Park/South Gyle: large secure warehouse-type buildings, security fencing, and over 200 parking spaces for a facility with very few staff
principal_concerns.raised_by: Cllrs Joanna Mowat, Hal Osler, Kevin Lang, Amy McNeese-Mechan; APRS

principal_concerns.concern: Impact of the very high electricity demand on the grid and on existing and planned homes and businesses
Errors by the developer in independent environmental assessments

claimed_local_benefits.benefit: New publicly accessible park (relocated protected open space) fronting Lochside Court, with sports facilities, retained or increased in size versus the existing inaccessible green space
Supply of waste heat to homes and offices to be built at Edinburgh Park
Active travel routes (east-west pedestrian/cycle route along the south of the site), landscaping and urban greening/biodiversity measures

stakeholder_positions.position: Opposed; called the refusal 'an absolutely momentous decision' and demands a Scottish Government moratorium on hyperscale data centres pending review; active party in the appeal

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: City of Edinburgh Council planning officers
stakeholder_positions.position: Recommended approval in principle, while noting the absence of any definition or glossary entry for 'green data centre' and advising members it was 'in their gift' to weigh national development status against other material considerations

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: Development Management Sub-Committee (all parties: Green, Conservative, Lib Dem, SNP, Labour members present)
stakeholder_positions.position: Unanimously refused; key quotes: 'we've been told there is something in place but we haven't been given the figures' (Mumford, on renewables); 'If you look at guidance on green data centres - who the hell knows?' (Mowat)
Supports the council's request for national guidance defining 'green data centres'; critical of green claims lacking evidence, without formally opposing the scheme
Opposed; mobilising representations against the appeal

Councillors backed moves towards a temporary ban/moratorium on AI data centres in March 2026, though officials warned a moratorium would be unenforceable since applicants can appeal to the Scottish Government
Recalled appeal PPA-230-2794 on 17 August 2026 for ministerial consideration; the DPEA case is on hold.

campaign_groups: South Gyle local residents' campaign group (informal)
notes: Consultation_deadline shown is the DPEA appeal representations deadline (28 April 2026), now passed. Objection counts at application stage could not be established.
